requirements.name: Cultural and Social Perspectives on Sustainability: 6 units
requirements.raw_text: Cultural and Social Perspectives on Sustainability: 6 units

courses.title: Environment and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Environmental problems related to use of natural resources by modern societies. Issues discussed include availability of food, water, and energy by a rapidly growing world population, and the effects of pollution, climate change and decreasing biodiversity on ecosystems and societies. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Equity Issues in K-9 Environmental and Science Education Service Learning
courses.description: Diversity, equity, and inclusion in diverse K-9 environmental and science education contexts, including classrooms, afterschool programs, and non-profit organizations like urban farms. Embracing CPP’s “Learn by Doing” philosophy, students have the opportunity to apply their knowledge in real-world education settings by designing and teaching lessons at local school gardens and farms. Structural biases in environmental and science education, with a special emphasis on the urban K-9 US context. Examination of the history of environmental and science education in schools considering students’ cultural, race, and gender/sexuality backgrounds. Critical analysis of contemporary curricula, frameworks, developing strategies to effectively create an equitable and inclusive classroom. Explore concepts, theories, and frameworks in critical environmental and science teaching, such as culturally relevant pedagogy, that will provide students with concrete tools to use in their future careers as educators.
courses.prerequisites: LS 2011 and LS 3011 .

courses.title: Liberal Studies Synthesis Interdisciplinary Perspective on Contemporary Public Education
courses.description: Explores varied perspectives on public education to analyze its purpose and effectiveness on student outcomes and lives. Discuss major issues in public education, with a focus on inequality, social justice, and civic engagement, using knowledge in the humanities and social sciences, and natural science when appropriate. Develop a complex understanding of the relationship between schools and society through interdisciplinary thinking. Service-learning at department public school partner or community partner site is required.
courses.prerequisites: Senior standing, LS 201 or LS 2011 , LS 301 or LS 3011 , LS 3021 , LS 3031 , LS 3041 , LS 401 or LS 4011 , and LS 421 or LS 4211 .

courses.title: Sociolinguistics
courses.description: [GE 4C] The study of language use in society and of mutual influences of society and language. Focus on regional and social dialectology, language ideology, language and social categories (gender, ethnicity, social class).
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Cultures of Childhood
courses.description: Identifies how different cultures/ethnic groups conceptualize childhood and how they construct the culture, cultural artifacts and practices for children. It identifies theories and examines early childhood development and practices within diverse families and communities. Explore the development and demonstration of culturally competent communication and the promotion of social justice for young children and their families.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or Senior Standing.

courses.title: Education and Social Change
courses.description: Comparative theoretical and empirical overview of historically marginalized student educational issues in the United States, with special emphasis on analyzing the effects of race, gender, class, sexuality, and immigrant status on historically marginalized student’s educational attainment and achievements. An examination of how historical, social, political, and economic forces impact their educational experience. Pays specific attention to the active roles that students, parents, and communities have in educational advocacy and social change.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or Senior Standing.

courses.title: Arts in Action
courses.description: Utilizing critical thematic pedagogies and engaged student works, this course focuses on arts integration with other disciplines in the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences to develop an awareness and commitment to social justice through the arts. Students can expect to develop an understanding and appreciation of the interdisciplinary arts and to explore the critical role of the arts in education, community engagement, and in building sustainable environments, ecologies, cultures, and societies.
courses.prerequisites: LS 201 or LS 2011 , LS 301 or LS 3011 , LS 3021 , LS 3031 , LS 3041 , LS 401 or LS 4011 , and TH 423 or TH 4230 .

courses.title: Critical Performing Arts and Education
courses.description: Examines performing arts (dance, movement, music, ritual, sound arts, storymaking, theater, and other time-based works), media arts (film, video), and their interdisciplinary integration with the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. Employs critical thematic pedagogies and engaged student work to apply artistic practice to questions of social justice. Emphasizes interdisciplinary performance, arts advocacy, education, community engagement, and the role of the arts in fostering sustainable environments, ecologies, cultures, and societies.

courses.title: Sustainable Fashion
courses.description: The impact of apparel and textile production and consumption on the environment. Exploring the possibilities of a more environmentally responsible approach to fashion production and consumption from fiber production to the end-use and re-use of apparel products. Corequisite(s): AMM 2150A .

courses.title: Sustainable Fashion Activity
courses.description: The impact of apparel and textile production and consumption on the environment. Exploring and evaluating more environmentally responsible approaches to fashion production and consumption through written and practical projects. Corequisite(s): AMM 2150 .

courses.title: Life Science for Elementary Educators
courses.description: [GE 5B] Introduction to life science, including biological processes (from molecules to ecosystems), the relationship between form and function, reproduction, heredity, evolution, and impact of humans on other organisms. Introduction to modeling effective K-8 curriculum and teaching and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. Corequisite(s): BIO 2120L .

courses.title: Life Science for Elementary Educators Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Inquiry-based, hands on activities and investigations of biological processes from molecules to ecosystems, relationship between form and function, reproduction, heredity, evolution, and the impact of humans on other organisms. Modeling of effective K-8 curriculum, teaching and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. Lecture and lab are integrated closely modeling elementary science teaching. Corequisite(s): BIO 2120 .

courses.title: Biodiversity Conservation
courses.description: [GE 5D] Course addresses global patterns of biological diversity, the impact of humans on natural systems and diversity, and use of scientific principles to protect and restore diversity. Open to all majors. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Marine Biology
courses.description: [GE 5D] An overview of the marine physical environment and the organisms that inhabit it. Emphasis on the interconnections between the ecology of the oceans and the rest of the biosphere, including human activities. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Interpretation of Science Service Learning
courses.description: Methods and techniques necessary to develop professional oral interpretive skills in the sciences. Students will design and develop formal interpretive nature walks that enhance their audience’s understanding and appreciation of science and nature. Corequisite(s): BIO 4910AS .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L .

courses.title: Climatology
courses.description: [GE 5D] Introduction to the fundamental concepts and theories in climatology. Methods of inquiry, including qualitative, quantitative, and computer based modeling and simulation methods. Explore climate variation through time and space and the reciprocal impact of climate and society. 3 hours lecture/problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Climate Change: Science and Action
courses.description: In depth investigation of the science of global warming and humankind’s impact on the Earth’s climate system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3070L .
courses.prerequisites: One course in GE Area B, GEO 1010 , GEO 1010L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Climate Change: Science and Action Laboratory
courses.description: In depth investigation of the science of global warming and humankind’s impact on the Earth’s climate system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3070 .
courses.prerequisites: One course in GE Area B, GEO 1010 , GEO 1010L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
courses.description: Principles and techniques of remote sensing using remotely sensed data to examine physical and cultural geographic scenes. Remote sensing applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecosystem management, atmosphere and earth sciences, and geographic information systems. Corequisite(s): GEO 4100L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Principles and techniques of remote sensing using remotely sensed data to examine physical and cultural geographic scenes. Remote sensing applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecosystem management, atmosphere and earth sciences, and geographic information systems. Corequisite(s): GEO 4100 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L .

courses.title: Environmental Modeling with GIS
courses.description: Environmental modeling within the geospatial framework. Theoretical foundations and technical approaches to model development with GIS. Issues and applications associated with environmental models. 2 hours lecture/problem-solving. Corequisite(s): GEO 4450L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Environmental Modeling with GIS Laboratory
courses.description: Environmental modeling within the geospatial framework. Theoretical foundations and technical approaches to model development with GIS. Issues and applications associated with environmental models. 3 hours laboratory. Corequisite(s): GEO 4450 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Planet Earth: A Citizen’s Guide
courses.description: Development of knowledge pertinent to Earth stewardship and global citizenship, with emphasis on building and maintaining a habitable earth. Survey of issues such as climate change, environmental and natural hazards, water resource development and conservation, and/or environmental sustainability, with their social, emotional, financial, psychological, and physiological impacts. Corequisite(s): GSC 1010A .

courses.title: Planet Earth: A Citizen’s Guide Activity
courses.description: Activities directed toward educating regional or campus communities about response to / recovery from challenges posed by Earth’s environment. Enhancement of skills to evaluate such challenges, engage in related conversations, and promote community awareness. Participation in events such as Earth Day, California Shake-Out, and disaster preparedness drills. Promotion of water conservation and waste recycling. Outdoor field trips. Corequisite(s): GSC 1010 .

courses.title: Water in a Changing World
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to water resource issues affecting urban, agricultural, and natural end-users in California, and the arid southwest. Integrates basic hydrologic principles, discussion of recent research, and historical issues to understand current water resource management decisions and future trends in water use.

courses.title: Earth Science for Elementary Educators
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to Earth Science including: physical and planetary geology, weather and climate, and human impact on Earth’s systems. Modeling of effective K-8 curriculum, teaching and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. Corequisite(s): GSC 2120L .

courses.title: Earth Science for Elementary Educators Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory activities in Earth Science including: physical and planetary geology, weather and climate, and human impact on Earth’s systems. Modeling of effective K-8 curriculum, teaching and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. Fieldwork component is required. Corequisite(s): GSC 2120 .

courses.title: Studies of a Blue Planet
courses.description: [GE 5D] Science-based issues related to the ocean-atmosphere system that directly impact humans. Global environmental change, El Nio/La Nia, ozone depletion, sea level changes, coastal development, alternative energy sources and satellite monitoring of earth are investigated. Individual or team research presentations describe selected linked ocean-atmosphere phenomena or case studies.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Exploring Earth’s Oceans: Oceanography
courses.description: [GE 5D] Scientific investigation of fundamental processes emphasizing physical, chemical, and geological oceanography. Topics include currents, tides, waves, beaches, chemistry of ocean water, ocean basin evolution and physiography, sedimentation, coastal hazards, marine climate, and relevant marine biological processes. Independent field trip. Individual or team presentations describe selected oceanographic phenomena or case studies.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Physical Science for Elementary Educators
courses.description: Introduction to physical science concepts including forces, matter and its interactions, energy, physical properties of materials, physical changes, chemical reactions, conservation of mass, small particle theory, and wave properties and applications. Modeling of effective K-8 curriculum, teaching, and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. The course includes a fieldwork component. Corequisite(s): PHY 2120L .

courses.title: Physical Science for Elementary Educators Laboratory
courses.description: Inquiry-based, hands-on activities and investigations of physical science concepts including forces, matter and its interactions, energy, physical changes, chemical reactions and conservation of mass, small particle theory, and wave properties and applications. Modeling of effective K-8 curriculum, teaching, and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. The course includes a fieldwork component. Corequisite(s): PHY 2120 .

courses.title: Energy and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Study of how petroleum, solar, nuclear, and other energy sources generate electricity, power vehicles, and the like. Emphasis is on elementary physics principles. Coverage includes historical patterns of societal energy use, renewable and nonrenewable resources, fuel conservation methods, and environmental impacts.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650L .

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture Laboratory
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650 .

courses.title: Urban and Community Agriculture
courses.description: [GE 5D] An integration of production methods and technology, social enterprise, and emerging business models for urban agriculture. Emphasis on growing, distributing, and marketing food and other products within metropolitan areas. Topics include community and school gardens, backyard plots, rooftop gardens, aquaponics, hydroponics, vertical farming and more. Attention to community development components of urban agriculture. Lecture, discussion, urban farm case studies and guest speakers with an emphasis on Southern California.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Small-Scale Sustainable Farming
courses.description: The diverse components of agricultural production on a small scale. Examine a number of existing small scale production models. Critically analyze small-scale production systems to determine how well they achieve economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity. Corequisite(s): PLT 4965L .

courses.title: Small-Scale Sustainable Farming Laboratory
courses.description: Engage in practical activities covering soil health, composting, crop planning, and integrated pest management. Emphasizing sustainable techniques in small-scale farming, the course fosters teamwork and critical problem-solving skills, preparing students to apply sustainable practices in real-world settings. Corequisite(s): PLT 4965 .

courses.title: Life Support Processes
courses.description: [GE 5D] Understanding the complex physical and biological systems, and the social context within which they occur, which provide resources and processes to meet the basic needs of human communities. These systems and processes provide water, food, energy, shelter, atmosphere, and a functional landscape.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Global Resources for Food
courses.requirement: Cultural and Social Perspectives on Sustainability: 6 units
courses.description: [GE 4A] Examine the resource base for agricultural production on various continents, and whether there is potential for increasing food supplies. The role of agriculture in economic development will be addressed.

courses.title: Race, Ethnicity and Food Justice
courses.requirement: Cultural and Social Perspectives on Sustainability: 6 units
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2050 Examination of racialization and erasure of the histories of Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and/or Latina and Latino Americans communities in the US with regard to food and agriculture. A foundational understanding of the history of oppression of minorities and policies that have kept these groups marginalized within the Agriculture industry will be investigated. Current food justice movements that aim to solve long withstanding and historical problems within society will also be studied.

courses.title: Race, Ethnicity and Food Justice
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: AG 2050 Examination of racialization and erasure of the histories of Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and/or Latina and Latino Americans communities in the US with regard to food and agriculture. A foundational understanding of the history of oppression of minorities and policies that have kept these groups marginalized within the Agriculture industry will be investigated. Current food justice movements that aim to solve long withstanding and historical problems within society will also be studied.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity in Fashion
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 1090 Fashion and race in the context of social, cultural, and environmental influences in the US. A focus is placed on members of historically racialized groups in the US including Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latino American communities who are active producers and consumers of apparel. Apparel and textiles will be critically examined with attention to racial formation discourses as they relate to ethnicity, race, nation, class, culture, social movements, environmental-health disparities, and policy. This course is administered as a flipped course that consists of lectures, readings, discussions, a group project, and presentations.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity in Fashion
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: AMM 1090 Fashion and race in the context of social, cultural, and environmental influences in the US. A focus is placed on members of historically racialized groups in the US including Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latino American communities who are active producers and consumers of apparel. Apparel and textiles will be critically examined with attention to racial formation discourses as they relate to ethnicity, race, nation, class, culture, social movements, environmental-health disparities, and policy. This course is administered as a flipped course that consists of lectures, readings, discussions, a group project, and presentations.

courses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and the American Consumer
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 1250 Examine how race and ethnicity has been constructed in the US, and the impact of racial stigma and discrimination in the retail marketplace as it relates to consumer behavior. Consumer processes and motives will be investigated with reference to the intersection of race and ethnicity with other demographic and behavioral characteristics - with a focus on African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans, and Latina and Latino Americans. Topics will include social constructs of race, racism in the consumer market, marketplace discrimination, consumer inequality, stereotyping, sustainability, and consumer rights. Lecture/discussion, case studies, analysis of datasets, and a student project related to race and consumerism in America.

courses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and the American Consumer
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: AMM 1250 Examine how race and ethnicity has been constructed in the US, and the impact of racial stigma and discrimination in the retail marketplace as it relates to consumer behavior. Consumer processes and motives will be investigated with reference to the intersection of race and ethnicity with other demographic and behavioral characteristics - with a focus on African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans, and Latina and Latino Americans. Topics will include social constructs of race, racism in the consumer market, marketplace discrimination, consumer inequality, stereotyping, sustainability, and consumer rights. Lecture/discussion, case studies, analysis of datasets, and a student project related to race and consumerism in America.

courses.title: Environment, Technology and Culture
courses.description: [GE 4C or 5D] Student focused investigation of the interrelationships between a society’s subsistence and economic systems, level of socio-cultural development, and the natural and social environment inhabited. Tools and techniques utilized by particular societies in their exploitation of their surroundings.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: The Japanese American Experience and the California Landscape
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: LA 2250 Investigates the intersection of ethnic studies and landscape architecture by exploring the relationship between the Asian American community and place in the United States. Through the lens of the Japanese American experience in California since the late 19th century, this course will examine topics that include immigration patterns, socio-economic and political factors shaping US immigration policies, racism and its connection to labor and employment practices with focus on landscape and agriculture, World War II internment, post-war era ethnic resilience, the role of environmental influences in individual well-being, and evaluation of cultural identity in the Asian American community. Field trips are required.

courses.title: Contemporary African American Studies
courses.description: [GE 4C] Critical and interdisciplinary analysis of contemporary African American communities by synthesizing perspectives from the social sciences and humanities. Topics include economic status, education, gender, identity, prisons, migration, citizenship, law and public policy, communities, religion/spirituality, health, politics, pan-ethnic identities, social justice movements, environmental justice, self-determination, popular culture and media representations.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Contemporary Chicana/o and Latina/o Studies
courses.description: [GE 4C] Critical and interdisciplinary analysis of contemporary Chicana/o and Latina/o communities by synthesizing perspectives from the social sciences and humanities. Topics include economic status, education, gender, identity, prisons, immigration, citizenship, law and public policy, communities, religion/spirituality, health, politics, pan-ethnic identities, social justice movements, environmental justice, self-determination, popular culture and media representations.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Contemporary Native American Studies
courses.description: [GE 4C] Critical and interdisciplinary analysis of contemporary Native American communities by synthesizing perspectives from the social sciences and humanities. Topics include economic status, education, gender, identity, prisons, federal and state policies, tribal governance, systems of oppression, reservations, communities, religion/spirituality, health, politics, activism and social justice movements, environmental justice, self-determination, popular culture, art, and media representations.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Contemporary Asian Pacific Islander American Studies
courses.description: [GE 4C] Explores contemporary Asian Pacific Islander American issues including US immigration policies, Asian migration movements, divers ethnic traditions within Asian America, employment, education, family, ethnic resilience, inter-ethnic and intra-Asian relationship, pan-Asian identity, social justice, race relationship and media representations of Asians and Asian Americans examined from perspectives of history, sociology, cultural/ ethnic and gender studies.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Gender, Power, and Emerging Technologies
courses.description: [GE 4C] Examination of the interrelationship between identity, power and technological competency while addressing the acceleration of technological innovation and dissemination. Using perspectives from ethnic, gender, and sexuality studies, history, sociology, cultural studies, and political activism, students will explore connections between access and mastery of technology with power and changing societal patterns. Analysis of the emerging technologies that continually restructure the local and global conditions of human experience by changing societal patterns. Corequisite(s): EWS 4250L .
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Gender, Power, and Emerging Technologies Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 4C] Examination of the interrelationship between identity, power and technological competency while addressing the acceleration of technological innovation and dissemination. Using perspectives from ethnic, gender, and sexuality studies, history, sociology, cultural studies, and political activism, students will explore connections between access and mastery of technology with power and changing societal patterns. Analysis of the emerging technologies that continually restructure the local and global conditions of human experience by changing societal patterns. Corequisite(s): EWS 4250 .
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Environmental Geography
courses.description: Explores geographic issues of natural resource availability, environmental consequences of patterns of population distribution, and pollution diffusing. Analysis of spatial patterns of human/environment impacts at regional and local scales. 2 hours lecture/discussion. Corequisite(s): GEO 3300L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 1010 or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Environmental Geography Laboratory
courses.description: Explores geographic issues of natural resource availability, environmental consequences of patterns of population distribution, and pollution diffusing. Analysis of spatial patterns of human/environment impacts at regional and local scales. Corequisite(s): GEO 3300 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 1010 or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Modern India
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] History of modern India’s transition from a British colony to the world’s largest democracy. Interactions among the forces of tradition and modernity, colonialism and nationalism, communal separatism and national integration. Challenges to democracy, development, social justice, and ecological sustainability in independent India.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Introduction to Public and Applied History
courses.description: Principles, techniques, and ethical issues of history in a non-academic setting. Production and dissemination of history in museums, archives, historical sites, business, and media with an emphasis on theoretical and practical issues.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Modern Science in World History
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Intellectual, philosophical, cultural, technological, political, and transnational origins and impact of the scientific revolution in the world in the 20th century and beyond. Rise of relativity, quantum and nuclear physics, computers, internet, genetics and molecular biology, Cold War science, and climate change.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: History of American Science and Technology
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Social, political, economic, and cultural shaping and impact of American science and technology from colonial period to the present. Science in government, industrial revolution, technological systems, Taylorism, atomic bomb, Cold War, environmental movement, computer, internet, social media, biotechnology, and climate change.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Environmental History
courses.description: Global and local themes in modern environmental history, including the historical interrelationship between humans and the natural and built environment, development of modern environmental ideas in society and social movements centered on environmental concerns.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Ethnic Studies of Food, Nutrition, and Health Disparities
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2180 Interdisciplinary study of Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities and food, nutrition, and health inequities in the United States. Foundational theoretical concepts of ethnic studies and nutrition such as racism, colonialism, immigration, eurocentrism, social determinants of health, food and health disparities, acculturation, and health equity are examined.

courses.title: Urban Agriculture Policy and Community Development
courses.description: Explores the emerging urban agriculture movement and policy initiatives that promote farming in the city. Examination of existing laws and policies, impact on urban farming, and policy development and implementation, to develop skills in communicating with decision makers. Engagement in a practicum on a local urban agriculture policy issue. Includes guest speakers and field trips that highlight local urban farming and related policy development. Corequisite(s): PLT 4975L .

courses.title: Urban Agriculture Business Models
courses.description: Introduction to the characteristics of urban agriculture business models and the knowledge required to start an economically sustainable urban agriculture business. Exploration of resources and support to urban farmers. Students develop a business plan focusing on existing or proposed urban agriculture enterprise.

courses.title: Organization for Regenerative Practices
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Investigation of sustainable organizing processes for regenerative practices. The cultural and institutional organizing processes are examined at the global, multi-national, national, regional, local, family, and individual levels. Organizing practice is examined in the context of coalitions among government, business, community and environmental groups, and evaluated with regard to effectiveness in advancing pro-environmental change.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Sustainable Communities
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Interdisciplinary and cross cultural study of sustainable communities, emphasizing the interdependence of human society and ecology expressed in built form. Examination and analysis of intentional communities as models of traditional and/or alternative patterns. Exploration of legal and economic organization of land holding patterns, housing and community design features and values inhibiting or facilitating experimentation. Explores the impact of cultural values in our interpretation of science and history.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Introduction to Science, Technology, and Society
courses.description: [GE 3B] Examines the interrelation among science, technology, and society. Emphasis on historical and current cases that help characterize the nature of science, and on the involvement of values in science and technology.

courses.title: Peer Theatre I
courses.description: Theories and practical teaching methods of Peer Theatre and Theatre for Youth. Service learning component where students work with regional school districts in the creation of an original play. May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: Junior Standing.
